title: PRD: Multi-Mode Endpoint Adapter (chat/completion/embedding/rerank) + Launch Checklist
creator: Aisha Raman
background: We currently expose separate endpoints and behavior patterns for chat, completion, embeddings, and rerank. This PRD defines a unified adapter layer (multi-mode endpoint) that allows a single hosted endpoint to accept a mode parameter and route/transform requests to mode-specific runtime code paths while preserving backward compatibility for existing customers.
goals: Provide a single /v1/infer endpoint with explicit mode: chat|completion|embedding|rerank
Keep existing endpoints operational and provide migration guidance
Ensure per-mode SLOs (latency, error rate, token cost) are met under hosted SLAs
Support streaming for chat/completion without degrading embeddings/rerank behavior
Ship a rollout and rollback plan with observability and automated fallback to legacy endpoints
non_goals: Replace existing SDK surface in the initial launch; SDK changes to be a follow-up
Aggregate embeddings across calls (batching improvements will be handled by Optimize project)
Revamp auth or billing model as part of this change
requirements: API contract: POST /v1/infer { "mode": <string>, "model": <string>, "input": <object> } with mode required

Mode behaviors: chat -> supports messages array, function calls, streaming; completion -> prompt+params+streaming; embedding -> accepts texts/inputs, returns numeric vector; rerank -> accepts candidates and query, returns ranked list with scores
Backward compatibility: existing endpoints (/v1/chat, /v1/completions, /v1/embeddings, /v1/rerank) must continue to work unchanged for 90 days after GA
Runtime routing: adapter must route to optimized runtime kernels (quantized variants when available) and not increase median latency by >10% for any mode
Observability: expose per-request metadata (mode, model, token_count_in/out, routing_variant) to tracing and metrics
Quota & Rate-limiting: adapter must honor customer-level quotas and route limits and surface correct 429 semantics per legacy behavior
Error semantics: preserve existing error codes and messages for legacy compatible behaviors; new adapter errors must map to documented codes
Privacy/Security: adapter must pass security review; request/response masking rules and PII redaction must be identical to legacy endpoints
Docs & Migrations: provide migration guide, quickstart snippets for curl/SDKs, and update Console UI to show multi-mode example requests
Testing: end-to-end tests for each mode including streaming, function-calling scaffolding, embedding dimensionality checks, and rerank ranking stability tests
Rollout controls: feature flag per region and canary percent control, with automated rollback on metric regression
acceptance_criteria: Contract tests: /v1/infer accepts mode and produces identical outputs to legacy endpoints for a representative test corpus (chat/completion/embedding/rerank) with <=0.5% deviation for nondeterministic models
Latency: P50 and P95 for each mode on representative load do not regress more than 10% compared to legacy endpoints; target P95s: chat < 850ms, completion < 700ms, embedding < 200ms, rerank < 400ms
Stability: Error rate (5xx) remains below 0.25% for each mode during 72-hour soak in canary region
Streaming correctness: chat/completion streaming behavior matches existing SDK semantics (chunk framing, event ordering, and early function-call triggers) validated by integration tests
Embedding integrity: returned vector dimensions and value ranges match model contract; randomized sample check against deterministic baseline
Rerank determinism: given same input candidate set and query under stable model variant, ranking order is consistent across 99.9% of requests
Fallback: When adapter fails (e.g., internal routing error), system automatically routes to legacy endpoint for requests from customers with legacy routing enabled and emits an incident event
Telemetry & Dashboards: per-mode dashboards (latency, errors, tokens, cost estimate) exist in Console with token-level breakdown and alert thresholds configured
Docs: migration guide, open API spec, and code examples published and linked from Console before broad rollout
Security: formal security review completed and signed off; any findings closed or triaged with mitigation before GA
rollout_plan: Alpha (internal): deploy adapter behind feature flag in staging; internal teams test for 2 weeks
Canary region: enable 5% traffic in us-west-2 for new customers only; 72-hour soak and metrics check
Expanded canary: increase to 25% traffic with a mix of traffic patterns and run 7-day soak
Gradual ramp: 25% -> 50% -> 100% for new signups over 4 weeks with monitoring gates
Legacy traffic migration: offer an opt-in migration API; after 60 days, begin rolling migration waves with communication and opt-out preserved
GA: full traffic switchover after 90 days of successful ramp and business sign-off
Rollback: immediate rollback to previous routing if alert conditions met (P95 latency +20% from baseline OR errors >1% absolute increase); rollback automatically disables adapter flag
risks_mitigation: Risk: Mode mis-specification by customers. Mitigation: fail-fast validation with clear error messages and example snippets in docs
Risk: Increased tail latency due to adapter overhead. Mitigation: microbenchmarks, kernel pinning per mode, and early A/B with p95 SLIs monitored
Risk: Regression in embedding dimensionality or rerank scoring. Mitigation: preflight contractual tests and deterministic baselines run as part of CI
Risk: Operational complexity in supporting both legacy and adapter flows. Mitigation: build transparent routing telemetry and a temporary compatibility shim that logs all routed requests
test_plan: Unit tests for request validation and mode parsing
Integration tests verifying parity with legacy endpoints (golden corpus)
Load tests per mode at target QPS using real traffic shape replay
Chaos tests: simulate runtime node failures and ensure automatic fallback to legacy endpoints
Security fuzzing and permission boundary checks
Manual UX review of Console examples and updated rate-limit messaging
launch_checklist: API spec finalized and published (OpenAPI and human-readable guide)
SDK examples added to JS/Python SDKs and smoke-tested
Console: example request templates for each mode and a migration CTA
Operational runbooks: canary monitoring, escalation path, and rollback steps documented
Billing: metering update completed and tested to ensure tokens are billed consistently
Observability: dashboards and alerts in place and verified against synthetic traffic
Legal & Privacy sign-off on data handling changes
Security review closed with any high/critical issues remediated
Support playbook and canned responses for common migration questions
Customer communications queued (blog post, in-console banner, emails for affected tenants)
notes: Design trade-off: We considered implicit mode inference (auto-detect chat vs completion) but rejected due to ambiguity and higher risk for breaking changes
We will measure early adopter satisfaction via NPS survey at week 4 post-migration for each wave
Plan to deprecate legacy endpoints only after 90 days post-GA and with customer opt-in windows explicitly enforced
final_notes_for_review: Seek cross-functional sign-off (Eng, Design, Security, Billing, Support) in the next planning sync. If any critical performance regressions appear during canary, pause ramp and assign ENG-oncall to remediation.
